body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not provide grants or contracts for direct services for infants and toddlers, for children in underserved geographic areas, and for children with disabilities, as required by 98.30(b)(1). (Plan Questions 4.1.1c and 4.5.1i). Please note the Lead Agency has an approved waiver for this requirement through August 1, 2026. Overall Target Completion Date: 08/01/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The Lead Agency is launching a Micro-Facility Pilot in early 2025. Each selected location will be eligible for up to 10 contracted slots to provide services to children in underserved geographic areas. 05/31/2025 2 The Lead Agency is currently working to develop models to determine supply and demand for CCDF vouchers in the state. Beginning July 2025, and each year thereafter, an assessment of needed supply will be determined and depending on fund availability, contracted slots will be used to boost supply for infants, toddlers and children with disabilities. The Lead Agency will be requesting a waiver to allow for the model to be developed and analysis completed. 08/01/2026

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency has not established a standard for the administration of medication consistent with standards for parental consent for license-exempt centers, license- exempt family child care providers, license-exempt in home care, or out-of-school programs, as required by 98.41(a)(1)(iii). (Plan Questions 5.3.3aiv, 5.3.3av, 5.3.3avi, 5.3.3avii, 5.3.3biv, 5.3.3bv, 5.3.3bvi, and 5.3.3bvii) • The Lead Agency does not require an annual inspection for license-exempt centers or license-exempt family child care providers for compliance with a standard for administration of medication consistent with standards for parental consent, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(ii). (Plan Questions 5.5.2ai and 5.5.2bi) Overall Target Completion Date: 12/31/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The lead agency is currently working on rule reform and has established an internal process to complete a first draft of new rules for all provider types. The update will establish a standard for the administration of medication consistent with standards for parental consent. The new rule will require a mandatory training on the topic to be complete in the 90 day orientation period for all staff. 03/31/2025 2 As lead agency is working on draft, they will share with FSSA legal to cross reference with current regulations, Office of Child Care requirements and identity any gaps or amendments needed. 03/31/2025 3 FSSA legal team will draft rule language and review with lead agency for finalization and start the rule promulgation process. 12/31/2026 4 Lead Agency will update website, share communication with current providers of updated rules and update our data system with new rules. 12/31/2026 5 Lead agency will update licensing internal policy and licensing checklist to ensure that this standard is being checked on all annual and renewal inspections. 12/31/2026

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency has not established a standard for building and physical premises safety, including the identification of and protection from hazards, bodies of water, and vehicular traffic for licensed family child care providers, license-exempt centers, license- exempt family child care providers, license-exempt in-home care, and out-of-school programs, as required by 98.41(a)(1)(v). (Plan Questions 5.3.5bii, 5.3.5biv, 5.3.5bv, 5.3.5bvi, 5.3.5bvii, 5.3.5cii, 5.3.5civ, 5.3.5cv, 5.3.5cvi, and 5.3.5cvii) • The Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed family child care providers, or an annual inspection for license-exempt centers or license-exempt family child care providers for compliance with a standard for building and physical premises safety, including the identification of and protection from hazards, bodies of water and vehicular traffic, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B) and 98.42(b)(2)(ii). (Plan Questions 5.5.1bii, 5.5.2ai, and 5.5.2bi) Overall Target Completion Date: 12/31/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The lead agency is currently working on rule reform and has established an internal process to complete a first draft of new rules for all provider types. The update will establish a standard for building and physical premises safety, including the identification of and protection from hazards, bodies of water, and vehicular traffic for licensed family child care providers, license-exempt centers, license-exempt family child care. The new rule will require a mandatory training on the topic to be complete in the 90 day orientation period for all staff. 03/31/2025 2 As lead agency is working on draft, they will share with FSSA legal to cross reference with current regulations, Office of Child Care requirements and identity any gaps or amendments needed. 03/31/2025 3 FSSA legal team will draft rule language and review with lead agency for finalization and start the rule promulgation process. 12/31/2025 4 Lead Agency will update website, share communication with current providers of updated rules after rule promulgation and adoption of news rules are complete. 12/31/2026 5 Lead agency will update licensing internal policy and licensing checklist to ensure that this standard is being checked on all annual and renewal inspections. 12/31/2026

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency standard for emergency preparedness and response planning does not include all the required elements for licensed centers, licensed family child care providers, license-exempt centers, license-exempt family child care providers, license- exempt in-home care, or out-of-school programs, as required by 98.41(a)(1)(vii). (Plan Question 5.4.1g) • The Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers or licensed family child care providers, or an annual inspection for license- exempt centers or license-exempt family child care providers for compliance with a standard for emergency preparedness and response planning and with related pre- service or orientation training requirements, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B) and 98.42(b)(2)(ii). body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency has not established a standard for pediatric CPR for all staff in licensed centers, licensed family child care providers, license-exempt centers, license- exempt family child care providers, license-exempt in-home care, or out-of-school programs, as required by 98.41(a)(1)(x). (Plan Questions 5.3.10bi, 5.3.10bii, 5.3.10biv, 5.3.10bv, 5.3.10bvi, and 5.3.10bvii) • The Lead Agency does not require pre-service or orientation training on pediatric first aid and pediatric CPR, for licensed centers, licensed family child care providers, license- exempt centers, license-exempt family child care providers, or license-exempt in-home providers, as required by 98.44(b)(1)(i). (Plan Question 5.4.1j) • The Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers or licensed family child care, or an annual inspection for license-exempt centers or license-exempt family child care providers for compliance with a standard for pediatric CPR and with pre-service or orientation training requirements related to pediatric first aid and pediatric CPR, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B) and 98.42(b)(2)(ii). (Plan Questions 5.5.1aii, 5.5.1bii, 5.5.2ai, and 5.5.2bi) Overall Target Completion Date: 12/31/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The lead agency currently is going through an legislative update to include pediatric language as a requirement for CPR certification of staff. 03/31/2025 2 The lead agency is currently working on rule reform and has established an internal process to complete a first draft of new rules for all provider types. The update will establish a standard that require pediatric CPR for all staff in licensed centers, licensed family child care providers, license-exempt centers, license-exempt family child care. The new rule will require a mandatory training on the topic to be complete in the 90 day orientation period for all staff. 03/31/2025 3 As lead agency is working on draft, they will share with FSSA legal to cross reference with current regulations, Office of Child Care requirements and identity any gaps or amendments needed. 03/31/2025 4 FSSA legal team will draft rule language and review with lead agency for finalization and start the rule promulgation process. 12/31/2025 5 Lead Agency will update website, share communication with current providers of updated rules after rule promulgation and adoption of news rules are complete. 12/31/2026 6 Lead agency will update licensing internal policy and licensing checklist to ensure that this standard is being checked on all annual and renewal inspections. 12/31/2026

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency’s Statewide Disaster Plan does not include all required elements, as required by 98.16(dd)(2)(iii)(A) and 98.16(dd)(2)(iii)(B). (Plan Questions 8.5.1bii, 8.51biv, and 8.5.1bvi) Overall Target Completion Date: 10/01/2024 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 In 2023, the Lead Agency released an addendum to its Statewide Disaster Plan. The Background section of the addendum contains the following language: This Indiana Child Care Emergency Preparedness and Response Plan is not meant to replace any existing state of Indiana plans, but it is an adjunct or addendum to those plans. The Indiana Department of Homeland Security in conjunction with the Family Social Services Agency has written a separate overarching operational plan to ensure the continuity of operations plan for OECOSL and other FSSA divisions. This OECOSL- specific plan outlines the roles and responsibilities of OECOSL and key supporting agencies to prepare for, respond to and recover from a disaster that significantly impacts a community’s child care infrastructure. The terms ￿emergency￿ and ￿disaster￿ are used interchangeably and include both natural or human-caused events and other emergencies which may impact the daily business of child care. Both plans are found on the Lead Agency's website on this page: Emergency Response Planning for Child Care Providers The original, full plan is available here: https://www.in.gov/fssa/carefinder/ files/ Indiana_OECOSL_Emergency_Response_Plan_for_Child_Care_Support.pdf. The addendum is available here: https://www.in.gov/fssa/carefinder/files/ BCC_Indiana_Emergency_Response_Guide_for_Child_Care_Providers_COLOR.pdf 10/01/2024
